topics: overview of console trace inspector and request playback
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-21
Start: 16:21 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhao (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions Eng), Carlos Mendes (Redwood Product), Lena Ortiz (MarinerCare SRE), Dr. Marcus Hale (MarinerCare Head of ML), Olivia Park (MarinerCare Platform Eng), Jamal Rivera (MarinerCare Security)

[00:00] Samantha Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick round of intros? I'll hand it to Ethan to run the demo, I'll just kick off with context.
[00:22] Ethan Zhao: Hi all, Ethan here, SE on the inference team. Today we want to show the Console's request-forensics flow — from a high-level trace down to request playback and error root cause. We'll also highlight routing/fallbacks and KV cache behavior.
[00:45] Lena Ortiz: Great, we're most interested in how to quickly find which requests hit a degraded model variant and how to replay those requests offline. Our clinicians need predictable latency.
[01:05] Dr. Marcus Hale: Also want to understand quality regressions after quantization — how you'd surface that in the Console.
[01:17] Samantha Lee: Perfect. Quick pause — Jamal, any security constraints to flag up front?
[01:24] Jamal Rivera: HIPAA-adj, so we need encryption at rest, KMS, and audit logs. We're evaluating private deployment vs hosted with VPC peering. We'll need an HSM conversation if keys can't leave our control.
[01:40] Ethan Zhao: Noted. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we can present options — but we can go into the KMS/HSM details in the follow-up.

[02:05] Ethan Zhao: Switching into the Console — opening the Trace Inspector. You'll see a timeline of requests, color-coded by latency and error rate. (audio: mouse click) Sorry, the screen share is a little laggy.
[02:42] Ethan Zhao: So here at the top is the request map; selecting a request shows the full event chain — routing decision, model variant chosen, KV cache hit/miss, and if there was a fallback to a smaller quantized model.
[03:10] Olivia Park: That cache indicator — is that per-tenant or global?
[03:18] Ethan Zhao: Per-customer namespace by default. The Console shows both KV cache hits and prefix cache hits; we label them differently. In some transcripts the label is 'K-V cache' — we've seen that in a few exports.
[03:35] Lena Ortiz: And the fallback — will it automatically route to a compatible variant if the primary is out of capacity?
[03:43] Ethan Zhao: Yes, policy-driven. You can set ordinal fallbacks and cost/latency thresholds. In the trace you'll see a 'fallback' flag and the reason (e.g., capacity, error, or SLO breach).

[04:10] Ethan Zhao: I'm going to filter for requests with error codes and then group by session id. You can see a spike here around 14:12 UTC where errors jump.
[04:30] Dr. Marcus Hale: Can you show a generated diff of outputs pre/post-quant? We want to quickly see semantic drift.
[04:40] Ethan Zhao: We have a quality tab — it's tied to prompt sets and evals. Here I've got a small prompt set; we compare outputs and compute regressed metrics. In the Console it's surfaced as a percentage of prompts that exceed a semantic similarity threshold.
[05:05] Priya Nair: Quick note — the Console's eval view is integrated with Optimize recommendations, though the product naming sometimes shows 'Optimizer' in older builds.

[05:35] Ethan Zhao: Now I'll hit 'playback' on a single request. The system reconstructs the exact token sequence and model call including system messages, function calls, and streaming deltas.
[05:58] (audio: brief cross-talk)
[06:05] Olivia Park: When you replay, does it hit live backends or use recorded artifacts? We can't have patient data leave our VPC.
[06:15] Ethan Zhao: Two modes: sandbox playback that replays against recorded serialized inputs in the Console (no external network), and live replay that will re-execute to a model endpoint. For compliance you should use sandbox playback, which we recommend for any PHI-containing requests.
[06:39] Jamal Rivera: Good. Does sandbox playback still recreate KV cache state?
[06:46] Ethan Zhao: We snapshot the KV context when recording, so playback can simulate cache hits/misses. It's not an active cache callout.

[07:10] Samantha Lee: Let's walk through an example root cause — Ethan, can you surface the trace where fallback happened and show request logs?
[07:20] Ethan Zhao: Sure. Selecting that trace — you can see the request log shows a model error: 'inference oom' and then a fallback to 'gptx-quant-4' variant. There are per-token latencies and a stack of worker IDs so you can map to nodes.
[07:46] Lena Ortiz: Worker IDs — are those mappable to customer node IDs in Private?
[07:52] Ethan Zhao: Yes, in Private and Dedicated we surface node hostnames and instance types; for hosted we obfuscate raw hostnames but provide telemetry.

[08:18] Ethan Zhao: I'll open the console's error timeline — it links to related logs and a quick 'why' panel which aggregates possible causes (OOM, bad prompt, model regression, long input length). It's heuristic-driven with links to relevant spans in the trace.
[08:39] Dr. Marcus Hale: Are these heuristics tunable? We want fewer false positives.
[08:45] Ethan Zhao: Yes, the rule set is configurable in the Admin section and you can attach custom detectors or webhook alerts.

[09:10] (screen change)
[09:18] Ethan Zhao: Now demonstrating request log stitching. You can expand the request to see raw headers, API keys (redacted), and the exact prompt payload. There's a quick redact tool for PII/PHI before exporting.
[09:38] Olivia Park: That redaction — is it automatic? We need pattern-based PII scrubbing.
[09:45] Ethan Zhao: We include a set of regex rules and a safer default redact. You can also upload your own scrub rules in Private deployments.

[10:05] Priya Nair: On the topic of exports — we often get asked how to pull a subset of traces for offline analysis. We expose an API and S3 export. Ethan, show the export UI.
[10:20] Ethan Zhao: Export -> S3 -> pick timeframe -> choose sanitize -> export job queued. We also provide a pre-built lambda that masks PHI during export as a reference. Link in attachments.

[11:00] Lena Ortiz: About throughput, we peak at 200 QPS with some 1k spikes. How do the batching settings affect tail latency?
[11:12] Ethan Zhao: Good question. In the Optimize tab we show recommended batch sizes based on your sequence length distribution. There's a tradeoff: larger batches reduce per-token cost but increase tail latency. The Console has simulated curves for p50/p95/p99 given your traffic profile — I'll pull up a sample curve.
[11:40] (audio: mouse scrolling)
[11:50] Ethan Zhao: Here's a p99 bump when batch growth passes 16 due to queuing on the worker. We recommend a conservative batch size for low-latency clinical flows.
[12:05] Dr. Marcus Hale: Can we pin a version and have canary rollouts? We can't afford a regression in triage model.
[12:13] Ethan Zhao: Absolutely. The deployment layer supports pinning by route, canary slices, automatic rollback on quality regression thresholds, and multi-variant routing. The Console shows lineage and diff for model versions.

[12:40] Samantha Lee: Let's talk about pilot scope — we propose ingesting a masked week of request logs to run a bench and a quality check. Ethan will run a small job to estimate cost and latency under our infra assumptions.
[12:55] Ethan Zhao: For the benchmark I'll need sample request distribution (Olivia), sample prompt lengths, and a target SLO for p95. We will run a replay both against hosted and a local Dedicated-like profile.

[13:20] Olivia Park: I'll get the sample data and an anonymization script. We have some streaming function call logs we want to see in context.
[13:28] Ethan Zhao: Great, include any function specs. The Console also shows function call tracing and whether a function invocation caused an error.

[14:00] Jamal Rivera: On compliance: we need to see full audit trails and RBAC. Do we get token-level access logs?
[14:09] Ethan Zhao: Yes. Audit logs include token-level calls, admin actions, and export events. RBAC integrates with SSO (SAML/OIDC) and you can set route-level permissions.

[14:35] Samantha Lee: There's a security pack PDF in the attachments — I'll put that in the follow-up.
[14:44] Ethan Zhao: Quick demo of trace correlation: you can click a user session and the Console stitches all requests across time into a single timeline, useful for multi-turn chat when you want to see cumulative latency or when a function call failed mid-session.

[15:15] Dr. Marcus Hale: What about model explainability — can we see attribution for hallucinations?
[15:23] Ethan Zhao: We have preliminary tools: token-level attention snapshots and a 'likely hallucination' detector based on groundedness to a knowledge index. It's early but it's surfaced in the quality tab and linked in the trace.

[15:50] (customer question)
[16:00] Lena Ortiz: If we go Private, how long does the onboarding and data migration take?
[16:07] Priya Nair: Typically 4–6 weeks for the Private package including network setup, KMS integration and a security review. Dedicated is faster — around 2–3 weeks depending on approvals.

[16:30] Ethan Zhao: Back to the Console — I'll demonstrate a failure triage flow: mark a suspect request, add a note and tag engineers, then escalate to a runbook that triggers an alert channel.
[16:50] (audio: brief typing)
[17:00] Olivia Park: Can runbooks execute automated mitigations? For example scale up a pool or switch routing to a cheaper variant?
[17:08] Ethan Zhao: Yes, runbooks can be manual or automated. We have predefined actions like 'drain model pool', 'increase replica count', or 'change routing policy'. They can be gated by approvals.

[17:35] Samantha Lee: We sometimes see chunked transcription artifacts where names get mis-odered in exports — point to note.
[17:42] Ethan Zhao: Heh, yep. That's a common Fireflies-style mis-parse we see in sample exports.

[18:00] (screen: open network config)
[18:07] Ethan Zhao: For VPC connectivity we support private endpoints, IP allowlist, and peering. For on-prem we provide an installer and an air-gapped bundle.
[18:25] Jamal Rivera: If keys are in our HSM, can Redwood still verify request-level signatures?
[18:33] Ethan Zhao: Yes, we support RMS or sig-verification proxies. We can verify signatures without direct access to raw symmetric keys if you provide a verification endpoint. We'll detail that in the security doc.

[19:00] Samantha Lee: Ok, let's switch to a rapid Q&A before we close.
[19:08] Olivia Park: Question — do you have any built-in anomaly detection for sudden template changes?
[19:16] Ethan Zhao: Yup, we compare prompt embeddings across time and surface distributional shifts; alerts can be configured for drift thresholds.

[19:45] Lena Ortiz: If we need an SLA, does Redwood provide p99 latency SLAs for Dedicated?
[19:54] Samantha Lee: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated and Private; p99 guarantees are part of enterprise contracts. We'll include SLA language in the follow-up.

[20:10] Dr. Marcus Hale: About cost modelling — can you show an estimate per 1M tokens for our profile?
[20:18] Ethan Zhao: Quickly: using your average token lengths (~450 tokens) and 200 QPS peak, cost varies a lot by batch/quant. We'll produce a CSV with scenarios.

[21:00] (brief lull)
[21:08] Ethan Zhao: Wrapping up demo highlights: trace inspector, playback sandbox, error heuristics, export and redact, runbooks with automated mitigations, and canary/rollback.
[21:30] Samantha Lee: Recap of next steps — I'll send security packet and pilot pricing, Ethan will run a benchmark from masked logs, Olivia to share samples. We'll book the VPC deep dive with Jamal in next week.
[21:50] Jamal Rivera: Sounds good. Please include our legal contact on the security docs.
[22:00] Samantha Lee: Will do. Thanks everyone.

End notes:
- Shared links and attachments will be posted to the CRM and Slack channel.
- Minor transcription artifacts present (e.g., product nicknames like 'Redwood Optimizer' in older builds).
notes: Customer prioritized p95/p99 SLOs and HIPAA-adj security
Pilot to ingest masked request logs for bench and quality check
Follow-up deep dive on KMS/HSM and VPC connectivity
